name: arc-colored-block-rays
description: Use when ARC grids contain solid 3x3 color blocks. Extend each block's center row and column as full-grid rays, resolving crossings by color.
---

# ARC: 3x3 blocks emit colored rays

Use when a grid has multiple solid 3×3 square objects and scattered unrelated colored cells.

## Rule
1. Identify each uniform 3×3 block and its color. The center cell determines the ray origin.
2. Extend that color across the entire center row and the entire center column of the grid, retaining the block's cells and overwriting any scattered cells crossed by the rays.
3. At intersections of rays from different-colored blocks, leave the intersection cell 0 (background). If intersecting rays have the same color, keep that color.
4. Do not alter cells outside the ray rows/columns; scattered nonzero cells remain as they were.
5. Preserve the original grid dimensions.

## Verification
- Confirm all identified blocks have matching 3×3 dimensions and uniform color.
- Check every full ray across its entire row/column.
- Explicitly check ray crossings: different colors produce 0; same colors remain colored.
- Ensure unrelated cells outside rays are unchanged.

This procedure was verified on a demonstration where two 3×3 blocks emitted full horizontal and vertical rays, with their unlike-color crossing left blank.",
